In that same wide, your chip is already the one crimson chip in the warm-white field, and your pen stops and your head tips up to it by 5 to 6 s. Line 19 becomes 'A number. Over every head.' The close-up (your face, the chip with its 0.04% tag, your face again with eyes wide) lands on 'And yours says...'.

blockers.quote: A year of fees. A year of your life. On one chair. So... keep going?
blockers.why: Check #3, second hook by 0:30. On the draft's own clock the rule beat starts at 0:20. Lines 27 and 28 (about 8 s) and the 2 s hold at line 29 come first, so this line starts at about 0:30 and 'keep going?' lands at about 0:36. Your eyes drop from the chip to the fee receipt, go to the wall clock, then back up to the chip, over 'A year of fees. A year of your life. On that number. So... keep going?'. That lands by about 0:27, or about 0:23 with the opening trim. Lines 26 to 29 then answer it: 'What's that, in people? One chair. Out of two thousand five hundred.', with the hold on the pulsing chair. Put the fee receipt in line 15's set so it is in frame from the first second.

Wide on the stall: you in the apron, pouring, directly under the chaiwala's steady 61%; beside it your own crimson chip, its cards fluttering down from 0.04 to 0.02 with each cup; in the lit window above, the batch's chips tick up without you. Close on your face: you look up at your own chip, worried.' At about 2:07 this is roughly 40%. It also shows that a chip falls when its owner stops, which arms the drain a minute ahead.
